newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ABB says discussing Bakun dam, no dispute.
newsitem.headline: ABB says discussing Bakun dam, no dispute.

text.p: ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG said talks with Ekran Bhd about Malaysia's $6.18 billion Bakun hydroelectric dam project were part of normal discussions with any customer and should not be characterised as a dispute.
A company spokesman also said ABB did not comment publicly on such discussions, but it was confident the project would proceed as planned.

"We are confident that once the consortium -- ABB-CBPO -- is given the green light to start construction work, we will finish construction in the given time," an ABB spokesman said in response to inquiries.
The Bakun contract is the largest ever awarded to ABB and the value of the contract to ABB exceeds $2.5 billion.

ABB and joint contractor Brazil's Companhia Brasileria Projectos e Obras (CBPO) are waiting for preparatory work at the dam site, such as water diversion, to be completed before they can start work on their part of the project.

On Tuesday Malaysia's acting prime minister Anwar Ibrahim said there was a major dispute between Ekran, the main developer of the Bakun dam, and ABB over the terms of the agreement and this would lead to a delay in the project, due for completion by 2003.
He said he was referring to the project's $5.5 billion engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contract.
Earlier today in Kuala Lumpur, however, Ekran chairman Ting Pek Khiing played down the dispute and said the differences were not serious and were expected to be resolved.
The ABB spokesman echoed this view. "We would not call it a dispute. On large complex projects like this ongoing discussions are usual and expected," he said.

ABB's part of the project includes supplying six 420-megawatt hydro-generators, a 500-kilovolt high voltage direct-current transmission system, installing a 650-km submarine cable to connect the dam to peninsular Malaysia and civil works with CBPO.
The Malaysian government awarded the contract to Ekran. Ekran has a 32 percent stake in Bakun Hydroelectric Corp Bhd (BHEC), the project's operator, which is planning to float its shares.
